gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a named reviewer's measured battery runtime for any branded radio speaker. GadgetByte Nepal measured about 8 h from the JBL Tuner 2 over Bluetooth at full volume, against JBL's 12 h claim. Digital Radio Choice measured 14 h from the JBL Tuner 3 on DAB+ at moderate volume, and its review unit's USB-C port fractured the first time a cable was plugged in.
standout_why: I read three pages ChatGPT got: itechguides 'Best Bluetooth Speakers with FM Radio: 3 Top Picks', itechguides '10 Best … AM/FM', and powersof10 'Best Bluetooth Speakers with Radio 2026: Reviews & Tests'. Neither itechguides page measures anything; both say outright that controlled tests would be needed, and every figure on them is a maker or Amazon spec. The powersof10 author, Charles Eames, does give runtimes he measured himself: Antimi 11–12 h, BolaButty C27C 18–20 h, JEUJUG about 6 h at maximum volume. He states no method or test date, and he measures none of ChatGPT's card products (Avantree PowerByte, iHome iBT330, Avantree BoomByte, Tivoli Model One BT) and no JBL Tuner. So a measured runtime from a named outlet for a branded model is new, but the idea of a tested runtime is partly on a rival page already. I found no named measurement for any of the four products on ChatGPT's cards.
decides: This doesn't decide the pick. For the four card products I found only spec-sheet figures, no named measurement. Two outlets measured the JBL Tuner pair, and both results should be read as a warning. GadgetByte Nepal got about 8 of JBL's 12 claimed hours at full volume from the Tuner 2. Digital Radio Choice got 14 h on DAB+ from the Tuner 3, but that unit's USB-C port broke on first use. For radio quality, Jay Allen's verdicts are judgements in words, not figures, so a page can quote them only with his name attached. He rates the Sangean WR-16 'very sensitive to weak signals' on FM and the Avantree Soundbyte T FM 'pretty sensitive'.

findings.label: Measured battery runtime, Bluetooth, maximum volume
findings.value: about 8 h (JBL claims up to 12 h)
findings.note: Review published 2021-02-11, bylined 'Admin Writer'. Quote: 'I was able to get around 8 hours of playback time in Bluetooth mode… with the volume set at maximum the whole time.' That is 8/12 = about 67% of the claimed figure at full volume, from a single run.

findings.label: Measured charge time, 10 W charger
findings.note: Quote: 'I charged the speaker using my 10W Samsung charger and it took around 4 hours.' The same review notes distortion at the highest volume.

findings.label: Measured battery runtime, DAB+, moderate volume
findings.source_title: JBL Tuner 3 DAB+/FM radio speaker with Bluetooth – Digital Radio Choice
findings.note: Published 2026-03-14 by Digital Radio Choice; the byline is only 'Editor'. Quote: 'On battery power we were able to achieve 14 hours of listening to DAB+ radio stations.' The run was on DAB+, which US buyers can't receive, not FM or Bluetooth. FM: 'able to tune into all the FM stations we would expect to find.'

findings.label: Durability defect observed in test
findings.value: USB-C port fractured on first plug-in
findings.source_title: JBL Tuner 3 DAB+/FM radio speaker with Bluetooth – Digital Radio Choice
findings.note: Quote: 'The USB-C port on our JBL Tuner 3 fractured when we plugged in a lead for the first time.' One review unit.

findings.label: Measured Bluetooth range
findings.source_title: TEST: Tivoli Audio-Radios Model One BT, PAL BT und PAL+ – AREADVD
findings.note: Carsten Rampacher, AREADVD, published 2014-11-28 (an old test). 'fast 11 Meter werden geschafft' means 'nearly 11 meters are achieved'. FM reception is described only in words, 'gute Empfangssensitivität' ('good receiving sensitivity'), with the supplied antenna. No dB or frequency-response figures.

findings.label: FM weak-signal reception (named reviewer's judgement, not a number)
findings.value: 'very sensitive to weak signals although not quite as selective as the very best FM radios I compared it with'
findings.source_title: Sangean WR-16 / WR-16SE AM/FM Table Radio – RadioJayAllen
findings.note: Jay Allen, side-by-side listening against radios he doesn't name; no date on the page. AM: 'good sensitivity and is quite free of noise from the AC line.' He measured no battery runtime.

findings.label: FM reception (named reviewer's judgement, not a number)
findings.value: 'pretty sensitive' on FM, but 'does not match the FM reception of the best earbud-style radios' with the whip collapsed
findings.source_title: Avantree Soundbyte T streaming radio to earbuds (BTSP-860-T) – RadioJayAllen
findings.note: Jay Allen; no date on the page (its image paths suggest April 2025). This is the only named third-party reception test I found for any Avantree radio speaker. The 11 h battery figure on the page is Avantree's spec, not a measurement. It doesn't cover the PowerByte, BoomByte or SP850.

unsourced: TechRadar JBL Tuner 2 review: a search result said about 10 h of battery, but WebFetch got only the page title on two tries, so the figure is left out.
Avantree PowerByte (SP880): no named reviewer's measured battery, loudness or reception figure. Searched for reviews; found only Avantree's 20 h / 3600 mAh spec and owner comments.
iHome iBT330: no third-party review with measurements found.
Avantree BoomByte and Avantree SP850: no named measurement found. RadioJayAllen covers only the Soundbyte T among Avantree models.

Tivoli Model One BT: no measured SPL or frequency response found. The 87.7 dB average / 102.5 dB peak readings found belong to the Model One Digital (Wired), a different model, so they are left out. The Model One BT runs on mains power, so there is no battery runtime.
Sangean WR-16SE and PR-D4BT: no reviewer-measured battery runtime. The 36 h and 170 h figures are retailer specs.
RTINGS, SoundGuys and Notebookcheck: no review of any of these radio speakers found, so no lab figures from them.
Prices were not re-checked. This angle covers measurements only.
